Q1: Dispatch Call A (Maple St, 7.8) to the medic unit. Chest pain in a 68-year-old outscores the ankle (6.2) and the alarm activation (4.1), and none of the calls reaches the 9.0 threshold, which only governs escalation, not dispatch. A report of a person trapped on the 3rd floor with smoke showing (8.9) edges out the elevator rescue (8.8) as the highest-scored call, and the margin is real urgency, not a coin flip. Q8: Dispatch Call A (Cedar Ln, 8.7) to the medic unit. Stroke symptoms with a closing treatment window (8.7) clearly outscore abdominal pain (7.3) — time sensitivity is built into the score. Below 9.0 the unit dispatches normally; the threshold does not gate dispatch.
